title: GL Posting — a balanced double entry
description: The general-ledger document every accounting-committing family derives. Two invariants hold it together. The first is expressible in the schema and is enforced here: every line carries exactly one non-zero side, so a row is either a debit or a credit and never both or neither (the oneOf below). The second is a sum over the instance — total debits equal total credits — which JSON Schema cannot express, so the model enforces it as a declared family rule and refuses an unbalanced posting by name.

posting_date.description: The accounting date. The ledger a posting lands in is decided by this field, never by when the posting was written.

voucher_type.description: The document family this posting was derived from. Closed so a posting cannot cite a source the model cannot resolve.

voucher_id.description: The source document this posting is the ledger image of. Together with voucher_type it is the posting's provenance back into the transactional spine.

account.description: The ledger account the row posts to.

lines.description: At least two rows: a double entry needs both sides. Each row is exactly one of a debit or a credit.

harvest: the ledger row shape (account, debit, credit, cost center, posting date)
the voucher back-reference (voucher type and voucher id) that ties a ledger row to the document it images
double-entry as the invariant that makes a posting balanced or refused
x-erp-provenance.note: Field shapes from the upstream ledger doctype, re-expressed as one posting document with an explicit balance rule. No upstream file was read into this repository; no upstream code, schema or text is copied.
